A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Pianist Transformer work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and matchable despite substantial reformatting and reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original ASAP evaluations, a listening study with 39 retained participants, and pre-training, scaling, masking and architectural experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains those original empirical results and adds encoder-representation visualizations and transposition/tempo robustness results.

M1.justification: The eight-token MIDI representation, compressed 10-layer encoder/2-layer decoder, training objectives, pitch-constrained blockwise inference and Expressive Tempo Mapping algorithm remain unchanged. Expanded explanations do not establish procedural changes.

E1.justification: The pre-training datasets, ASAP evaluation and listening repertoire remain unchanged. V2 Section 4.5 adds evaluation under transposed and tempo-scaled inputs, extending coverage to a limited new perturbation scenario.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain ScorePerformer, VirtuosoNet-HAN, VirtuosoNet-ISGN, Score, Human and the existing model variants. V2 Table 3 summarizes the symmetric/asymmetric comparison already present in v1 Appendix F.

E3.justification: V2 introduces five perturbed variants per test score, using transposition from -6 to +5 semitones and tempo scaling from 0.7× to 1.3×, with matching reference transformations. Existing splits, training budgets and listening-study procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds two distinct diagnostics: t-SNE comparisons of supervised-only versus pre-trained encoder representations, and a perturbation test addressing generalization versus memorization. It removes v1's fine-tuning loss-curve analysis while retaining the quantitative pre-training ablation, scaling studies and appendix analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same paired t-tests and duplicate-stimulus bias/Pearson analysis. No seed, repeated-training-run or uncertainty-reporting practice changes are documented. The five perturbations are test variants, not repeated-run uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark and appendix table values remain unchanged. V2 Table 2 adds perturbed-input overall JS divergence of 0.1539 and intersection area of 0.8599; these are new-condition results, not improved same-setting scores. Figure 6 adds qualitative representation findings, while v1 Figure 3c's convergence results are removed.

T1.justification: The masked-denoising objective and sequence-compression mathematics are equivalent across versions. V2 clarifies the attention-matrix reduction without introducing new formal assumptions, definitions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The central scalable pre-training, efficiency and human-comparable rendering claims remain. V2 drops the introduction's explicit claim that pre-training accelerates fine-tuning and narrows the conclusion's stylistic-robustness attribution from a direct benefit to a promising potential benefit.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive interpretations involving style-organized representations, resistance to memorization and encoder quality as a downstream bottleneck. It also acknowledges possible pre-training/evaluation overlap, limited clips per style, classical-training biases and missing high-level controls. These substantially revise the explanations and applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1 expands the description of existing local velocity/timing augmentation. Appendix A.4 newly specifies IOI evaluation over 0-200 ms and duration over 0-500 ms. These disclose calculation details without establishing reruns. Resource directions are consolidated onto the project page.

R1.justification: V2 adds five 2026 references with brief appendix connections to structured representations, pretext-task transfer, multimodal benchmarking, robustness and test-time adaptation. The principal music-related survey and positioning against prior rendering methods remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract, contributions, experimental narrative and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Benchmark and listening results now precede the pre-training analysis, subsection organization changes, the appendix contents page disappears, and the ethics appendix becomes an expanded main-text Impact Statement.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from single-column to two-column layout. Figure 1 is redrawn, Figure 2 gains a legend, preference panels are restacked, and v1 Figure 3 is removed. V2 adds t-SNE and robustness displays plus a summary table redisplaying existing architectural results.

improvement.justification: V2 improves assessability by disclosing evaluation ranges, acknowledging overlap and genre limitations, and adding targeted robustness evidence. The gains are limited: headline results remain unchanged, convergence evidence is removed, and the t-SNE and perturbation analyses do not establish the proposed mechanisms or exclude memorization.
